summary.headline: Coverage gap: no Sentinel run for 26 days (last: 2026-06-30). MRVL/QCOM/CRDO persist RED on compounding valuation compression; MARA escalated AMBER→RED on SEC-filed insider selling plus deepening analyst target cuts. CWAN still undelisted in portfolios.json a month after first flagged. Dense earnings cluster ahead: NXPI 7/28, LRCX/QCOM/GD/AEM/HOOD 7/29, AMZN/COIN 7/30, AMD 8/4, VST 8/7, NVDA 8/26 — first hyperscaler data point (Alphabet, reported 7/22) raised 2026 capex guidance to $195–205B but still sold off ~3.7% on spend-intensity concerns.

flags.headline: MRVL -7.11% on the session; cumulative ~-38% off June 4 all-time high ($316.43 → $194.51)
flags.detail: Continues the AI-chip de-rating flagged since 2026-06-26. New this period: Benchmark analyst Cody Acree downgraded MRVL from Buy to Hold, citing reporting that Amazon shifted Trainium3/Trainium4 chip design work to Taiwan's Alchip Technologies — MRVL designed the earlier Trainium2 generation. Neither Marvell nor Amazon has confirmed this shift; the claim traces to Bloomberg-sourced reporting repeated by secondary aggregators (TradingView/GuruFocus), not a primary filing or direct tier-1 article — unconfirmed by tier-1 source, treat as a live risk to watch rather than a settled fact. Underlying FY2027 revenue guidance (~$11.5B, raised 2026-05-27) has not been revised down. Consensus remains Buy (28 analysts) and KeyBanc raised its PT to $400 on 7/14.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MRVL key_risk: 'Hyperscaler customer concentration — a small number of accounts (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft) generate the majority of AI-related revenue, and any shift toward fully in-house chip design or reallocation of custom silicon budgets could create material headwinds.' The Alchip design-loss reporting, if confirmed, would be this risk materializing at Marvell's largest custom-silicon relationship.

flags.headline: QCOM -2.43% on the session; ~-23% over the trailing month, worst stretch in years
flags.detail: Continues the decline flagged since 2026-06-26. Multiple analysts downgraded QCOM to Hold in early July following the June Investor Day, which highlighted execution and margin risk. Secondary reporting (via Bloomberg, not independently verified this run) describes QCOM signaling double-digit chip price increases tied to a DRAM/memory cost spike, against a backdrop of global smartphone shipments down 11% YoY in Q2 2026 (IDC/Canalys, via secondary reporting) — treat the pricing/memory claim as color, not confirmed, pending a direct tier-1 check. Q3 FY2026 earnings land 2026-07-29 (EPS consensus $2.22, down ~20% YoY) — the next hard confirmation point either way.
flags.thesis_link: Matches QCOM key_risk: 'Handset concentration at ~74% of QCT revenue creates vulnerability to smartphone market cyclicality' — a global smartphone shipment decline plus rising component costs is this risk playing out, pending 7/29 earnings confirmation.

evidence.source: Secondary reporting (Bloomberg via aggregators; not independently confirmed)

flags.headline: CRDO -9.73% on the session; down ~24% cumulative in under two weeks with no identified negative catalyst
flags.detail: Continues the decline flagged since 2026-06-26, now compounding: a 6-session slide erased ~$12B in market cap through 2026-07-20, and the 2026-07-24 session (-7.3% per MarketBeat) traded on volume 92% below average — consistent with a low-liquidity technical unwind rather than new fundamental news. No negative company-specific catalyst was found. Analysts have stayed bullish through the decline: Susquehanna raised its PT to $250 (from $235) and Barclays to $300 (from $260) in late July. The magnitude of the drawdown absent any confirmed cause is itself notable and worth the desk's attention — next earnings ~2026-09-09 (estimated, unconfirmed).
flags.thesis_link: Matches CRDO key_risk: 'Extreme valuation — 109x trailing P/E and 39x forward P/E... embed aggressive growth expectations, leaving minimal margin of safety for any execution miss or AI capex slowdown.' The multiple is compressing in real time even without a confirmed negative catalyst.

flags.headline: MARA -4.78% on the session; escalated from AMBER — repeated insider selling plus deepening analyst target cuts
flags.detail: Escalating from the 2026-06-30 AMBER flag (Q1 EPS miss). Insider Zabi Nowaid filed a new Form 144 to sell ~$100K of shares on 2026-07-21, continuing a pattern of insider sales in May and June 2026. Separately, Morgan Stanley cut its price target further to $5.50 (from $7, Underweight) against a $12.15 share price — implying analysts see over 50% further downside — following Bernstein's earlier cut to $17. A positive offset exists (a Texas power-site acquisition path to ~1GW by 2027 drove an 11-16% pop around 7/20-21), but the insider-selling pattern and the depth of the target cuts are the more material, escalating signal.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA key_risk: 'Persistent GAAP losses ($1.3B in Q1 2026 alone)... create existential risk if crypto enters a prolonged downturn and the company cannot service its $850M convertible debt obligations.' Repeated insider selling into a stock analysts see falling toward $5.50 is consistent with this risk deepening rather than resolving.

flags.headline: LRCX -4.48% on the session — broad wafer-fab-equipment selloff, no company-specific negative news
flags.detail: No stock-specific negative catalyst identified; consistent with a sector-wide semiconductor-equipment pullback also hitting KEYS/NXPI/ADI today. Analyst sentiment remains strongly positive (Morgan Stanley PT to $404, Evercore ISI to $355 in July). Q4 FY2026 earnings land 2026-07-29 — the next real test.

flags.headline: NXPI -2.97% on the session — continued automotive-chip softness, no new catalyst
flags.detail: Consistent with the automotive-demand softness already flagged; no new negative development found. Analyst actions are mixed-to-positive (BofA PT $310, Cantor Fitzgerald PT $400). Q2 2026 earnings land 2026-07-28.
flags.thesis_link: Matches NXPI key_risk: 'Automotive semiconductor demand is cyclical and tied to global vehicle production volumes.'

flags.headline: KEYS -1.99% on the session — valuation-driven pullback after a 106% run, no fundamental change
flags.detail: No new negative catalyst; Morgan Stanley upgraded to Overweight in mid-July and KEYS won a 3-year ESA blockchain-anomaly-detection contract. Q3 2026 earnings expected to show +40% YoY EPS growth. Reads as profit-taking on a stretched multiple, not deterioration.
flags.thesis_link: Matches KEYS key_risk: 'Valuation vulnerability at 49x trailing P/E and 30.5x forward P/E — any moderation in AI infrastructure capex could trigger significant multiple compression.'

flags.headline: HOOD -6.58% on the session — multiple compounding negatives: CEO account hacked, credit-expansion scrutiny, pre-earnings jitters
flags.detail: No single dominant catalyst; several factors stacked this week: (1) CEO Vlad Tenev's X account was hacked and used to promote a scam 'VLAD' token — reputational/security overhang, no financial impact identified; (2) Robinhood's first-ever asset-backed bond sale ($400-500M, backed by credit-card receivables) is drawing investor scrutiny as the company expands into consumer lending, credit-risk-appetite question; (3) ARK Invest sold ~$10.35M of HOOD shares on 7/22; (4) broader tech/crypto softness this week (Nasdaq -1.63%). Q2 earnings land 2026-07-29 (consensus $0.41 EPS / $1.21B revenue) — next confirmation point.
flags.thesis_link: The credit-expansion scrutiny touches on HOOD key_risk: 'Multi-front regulatory risk from SEC, CFTC, and state regulators... could constrain the fastest-growing product lines' — new lending/ABS activity is a new regulatory-scrutiny surface, not yet a confirmed problem.

flags.headline: GPC beat-and-raise on 7/22 earnings, but 2H guidance carries caution; unconfirmed ~$10B O'Reilly bid for NAPA/automotive business still in play
flags.detail: Q2 adjusted EPS $2.15 beat; FY adjusted EPS guidance reaffirmed at $7.50-$8.00, but GAAP EPS fell YoY on restructuring/separation costs and management flagged 2H cost pressure (tariff-related, softer European/NAPA independent-owner trends). Separately, reporting since 2026-07-02 describes a possible ~$10B cash bid from O'Reilly Automotive for GPC's NAPA/automotive segment — unconfirmed by either company, with a potential announcement flagged for 'late summer.' Today's +3.32% move likely reflects both the earnings beat and continued deal speculation.
flags.thesis_link: Matches GPC key_risk: 'Business separation execution risk — $225-250M in transformation costs, management distraction, and Moody's negative outlook create uncertainty around whether the breakup will actually unlock value or destroy it.' An M&A sale of the automotive segment would be a different path than the previously-thesised standalone separation — worth tracking, unconfirmed.

flags.headline: FCX beat EPS by 24% but cut 2026 Grasberg production guidance again — thesis key_risk continuing to materialize
flags.detail: Q2 EPS $0.74 vs $0.596 est, but FCX again lowered 2026 guidance at its Indonesian Grasberg mine — copper sales cut to 3.1B lbs and gold sales to 650,000 oz — citing continued wet-ore/drawpoint conditions requiring haulage infrastructure changes. This is a second cut on top of the ~11-13% single-day drop and Scotiabank downgrade that followed the Q1 2026 print. The muted -1.41% reaction (vs. the sharper Q1 move) suggests much of this is already priced in. Copper itself was flat (~$5.50+/lb) on the day, so this is company-specific, not a commodity move.
flags.thesis_link: Directly matches FCX key_risk: 'Grasberg execution risk — the September 2025 mud rush killed seven workers, triggered force majeure, and forced a 9% reduction in 5-year copper production guidance; underground block-cave operations face ongoing geological uncertainties as the restart progresses.' This is that risk continuing to play out in real time via a second guidance cut.

flags.headline: Hyperscaler capex earnings cluster imminent: MSFT/META 7/29, AMZN 7/30, NVDA 8/26 — first data point (GOOGL 7/22) mixed
flags.detail: Standing macro watch item continues. Alphabet reported 2026-07-22 (the first of the 'Big 5' to report since the last Sentinel run): raised full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B (from $180-190B), Q2 capex $44.9B (+100% YoY), Google Cloud revenue +82% YoY, cloud backlog +$50B in one quarter to $514B — but shares still fell ~3.65% after-hours on spend-intensity concerns, i.e. beat-and-raise wasn't enough to avoid a sell-the-news reaction. Microsoft and Meta report 2026-07-29, Amazon 2026-07-30, Nvidia not until 2026-08-26. Combined 2026 hyperscaler capex (ex-Nvidia) is tracking toward ~$700-725B, up from ~$410B in 2025 (~+77% YoY) per aggregated coverage. This remains the highest-priority macro signal for the AI-infrastructure-exposed holdings (MRVL, AMD, TSM, CRDO, LRCX, KEYS, NXPI, QCOM, NVDA).

flags.headline: SSNC +10.33% — guidance raise and record buyback drove the pop, not the EPS beat alone
flags.detail: EPS beat was modest ($1.76 vs $1.7125 est, +2.77%) and doesn't on its own explain a 10%+ move. Drivers: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $6.93-$7.25 (from ~$6.75 consensus) and revenue guidance to $6.672B-$6.832B; a record $499M / 6.4M-share buyback quarter under the renewed $1.5B program; and a new 'Blue Prism WorkHQ' agentic-AI product framed as a growth driver rather than a disruption risk this quarter. RBC raised its target to $92, Jefferies reiterated Buy at $83.

flags.headline: HUT -6.55% today reads as profit-taking after a major positive catalyst, not new negative news — resolved
flags.detail: The 2026-06-30 AMBER flag (merger settlement, new board chair) is stale and resolved — both were already-closed items even by that report. Since then, HUT signed a $9.8B, 15-year lease for phase two of its Beacon Point AI data center campus (announced ~7/20), which sent shares up as much as 17% and prompted Benchmark to raise its PT to $195 (from $165). Today's pullback tracks a broader bitcoin-miner sector give-back (RIOT also down) after that run, not any new adverse company development.

flags.headline: STLD +2.76% — Q2 print shows record shipments and a revenue beat; the margin-compression flag from 2026-06-30 is resolving
flags.detail: Q2 2026 EPS was a two-cent miss ($3.69 vs $3.71 est) but revenue beat sharply ($6.09B vs $5.68B est, +33% YoY) on record steel shipments (3.7M tonnes) and narrowing aluminum-segment losses. Analyst reaction was mixed but net positive (JPMorgan raised to $260 with a new Buy rating; Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley trimmed targets modestly). This looks like genuine improvement versus the guidance-miss/margin-compression concern flagged a month ago — downgrading to green pending confirmation next quarter.
